# Discover — list nearby knowledge bases without selecting one.

exec akb init project
stdout 'Initialized KB .project.'

exec akb init project-kb
stdout 'Initialized KB .project-kb.'

# A knowledge base nested two levels below the scenario root.
mkdir docs
cd docs
exec akb init kb
stdout 'Initialized KB .kb.'
cd $WORK

# Knowledge bases below skipped directories are not discovered.
mkdir .git/nested/.akb node_modules/nested/.akb vendor/nested/.akb .hidden/nested/.akb

# Discovery starts at the working directory and reports nearest first.
exec akb discover
stdout 'discovered knowledge bases \(nearest first\):'
stdout '^  project  [^\n]*\n  project-kb  '
stdout '(?s)  project-kb  .*  kb  .*/docs/kb'
stdout '^  kb  .*/docs/kb$'
stdout 'select one with --kb <path> or AKB_KB=<path>'
! stdout 'nested'
! stdout 'node_modules'
! stdout 'vendor'
! stdout '\.git'
! stdout '\.hidden'

# The scan can be rooted at an explicit directory.
exec akb discover docs
stdout '^  kb  .*/docs/kb$'

# Discovery is read-only: the addressed base stays clean.
exec akb --kb project status
stdout 'Git: clean'
exec akb discover docs
exec akb --kb project status
stdout 'Git: clean'

# The name comes from .akb.yaml, and its optional description is reported.
cp described.yaml project/.akb/.akb.yaml
exec akb discover
stdout '^  project  .*/project  project knowledge base$'

# JSON output pins names, paths, and the description.
exec akb discover --json
stdout '^\[.*\]$'
stdout '{"name":"project","path":"[^"]*/project","description":"project knowledge base"}'
stdout '{"name":"project-kb","path":"[^"]*/project-kb"}'
stdout '{"name":"kb","path":"[^"]*/docs/kb"}'

-- described.yaml --
name: project
description: project knowledge base
